housing: Portsmouth is England's most densely populated city outside London, built mostly on Portsea Island with rows of Victorian and Edwardian terraces. Southsea and Fratton have a large private rented sector, with many shared houses let to University of Portsmouth students and young workers, and every HMO in the city needs a licence. The city centre has post-war estates, towers and purpose-built student blocks, while Gunwharf Quays has modern waterfront apartments. On the mainland, Cosham, Drayton and Paulsgrove are mostly inter-war and post-war estates.
checkinTips: Shared houses in Southsea and Fratton: note the HMO licence number and photograph each bedroom lock, fire doors and closers, alarms and the shared kitchen and bathroom separately.
Seafront homes in Southsea and Eastney: record salt marks, rust on window fittings and damp on exposed walls.
Victorian terraces with small yards: photograph damp at the base of walls, rear yards and where bins are kept on narrow streets.
Waterfront apartments at Gunwharf: note fob counts, parking bays and balconies.
Low-lying streets near the harbours: photograph any damp low on walls and air bricks, as parts of the island can flood.
Converted Southsea villas split into flats: record communal hallways, meter cupboards and the key count for each door.
tenantHelp: Tenants can report disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions in privately rented homes to Portsmouth City Council's private sector housing team.
